idea-plugin.name: Flatpak DevTools
idea-plugin.description:
Build, run, and validate Flatpak applications from your JetBrains IDE. Flatpak DevTools turns flatpak-builder into a first-class workflow with dedicated Run Configurations and schema-aware editing — so you can develop and package sandboxed Linux apps without leaving your IDE.

Flatpak

  • Automatic manifest detection — manifest.json, flatpak.json, flatpak-manifest.json and app-id style files (org.example.App.json/.yaml/.yml) are bound to the official Flatpak schema automatically
  • Code completion & validation — schema-driven completion and inline validation for app-id, runtime, sdk, modules, finish-args, command and every other manifest field
  • One-click Flatpak actions — a dedicated Flatpak Run Configuration with Build, Run, Export, Clean, Validate and Custom commands
  • Smart project detection — Flatpak manifests are detected on project open with a one-time balloon offering to create run configurations; right-click any manifest to run Build <app-id>
  • Smart run — the Run command launches the built app inside the sandbox, executing the manifest's command (falling back to the app-id), with optional cleanup and portal sandbox flags
  • Flatpak Builder SDK integration — commands execute through the official org.flatpak.Builder SDK, with output streamed to the Run console
  • Configurable binaries — custom flatpak/flatpak-builder binaries, picked with a file chooser or typed directly in Settings

GtkBuilder XML support (premium, feature-flagged)

  • Code completion and validation for .ui/.glade interface files, driven by a GtkBuilder schema generated from the project's GNOME SDK
  • GNOME SDK autodetection — the schema branch follows the sdk/runtime declared in your Flatpak manifest, falling back to a bundled schema when no SDK is recognized
  • .xml files whose root element is <interface> are also supported once a Flatpak project is recognized
  • GTK snapshot preview — render the active .ui file to an image inside the GNOME SDK, with an editor notification and a dedicated preview tool window (Adwaita types render via a compatibility shim)

Known Issues

  • GTK Preview — Adwaita interfaces are not yet rendered correctly
  • Validate command in the JetBrains test sandbox — may report missing pip3/pipx; this is an artifact of the bare sandbox SDK, not of the command

GResource awareness (in progress)

  • WIP — notifying you when a UI file is not declared in your GResource manifest
